The repository’s format-check hook passed on retry. Nothing was pushed. The parallel v1 work remains in progress; its native-resolution test and independent review surfaced issues that still need follow-up.

Implement T03-PRE (Python prerelease baseline parsing), independently and in the shared worktree. Own only crates/callisto-model/src/format/pre.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/aggregate.rs, crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/pre.rs, crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/version.rs, crates/callisto-cli/tests/pre_mode_tests.rs. Read ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/architecture/versioning.md, docs/adr/README.md, relevant current specs and relevant code before changing behavior. Reuse the newly implemented Version::parse_for_ecosystem without changing pre.json format/schema. Resolve each baseline key to its historical/current owner using the established attribution rules; retain historical bare-key ownership and E245 ambiguity behavior. Add real regression coverage for stable Python pre enter/repeated version/exit and mixed SemVer siblings, qualified/unqualified keys, malformed values, custom changesets dir; coordinate with actual current contracts and don't invent unsupported semantics. Do not edit docs/specs/plan, changesets, Cargo.lock or other files. No Cargo builds/tests, no global formatter, no stage/commit; main owns serial verification. You are not alone in the codebase: preserve all other edits. Send main a progress note with any API/ownership uncertainty, then finish with files changed and sequential test command(s).

I’ll handle T03-PRE in the six assigned files, using the shared ecosystem parser and existing ownership rules. I’ll read the current contracts first, then add focused regressions for main’s serial verification queue.

I’m using Smith’s implementation workflow for this bounded change. The key risk is that a stable Python baseline such as `1.2.3` also parses as SemVer, so its owner must determine the grammar before prerelease planning uses it.

I’ll preserve orphaned entries and apply grammar correction after ownership resolution, then use that shared path for version planning and prerelease transitions.

The shared baseline resolver is implemented. Version planning, exit, and resume now resolve ownership before interpreting versions. The new regressions cover stable Python versions, Cargo/npm siblings, both qualified key spellings, historical promotion, E245 ambiguity, malformed values, and a custom changesets directory. I’m reviewing the fixtures now; main will run Cargo verification.
